Executive Briefing

Indian equity markets displayed robust performance for the week ending June 26, 2026. The Nifty 50 ended up 1.45% at 23,850, hitting historical highs driven by domestic retail SIP volumes and stabilizing private banking metrics.

Key Focal Points This Week
Sustained monsoon progress across Central India has significantly improved rural demand outlooks. Telecom sector tariff hikes of 10-15% executed by major players signal a return of premium pricing power, which has supported the heavyweights' earnings projections.
Institutional Stance
We advise maintaining a balanced asset mix. Target large-cap banking leaders and infrastructure companies that possess a solid valuation cushion, while trimming exposures in inflated mid-and-small-cap stocks.

Section 8: Case Study Page 14

Case Study: Titan's Trust Moat

In the 1990s, Indian jewelry retail was highly unorganized, characterized by under-carating and opaque pricing. Titan launched Tanishq in 1996 to address this, but initially struggled due to consumer habits. Titan solved this by introducing the Karatmeter—an X-ray tool to test gold purity for free. This built immediate trust and drove consumers away from unorganized jewellers. Today, jewelry contributes over 85% of Titan's revenue, demonstrating how building transparency in a low-trust market creates a structural competitive advantage.
Tanishq Trust Engine
Unorganized/Opaque gold retail market
Free Karatmeter testing introduced
Tanishq established as gold standard of trust
Investment Lesson
Companies that create transparency in unorganized markets often capture significant market share and build strong brand loyalty.
